core.title: Write every per-case covers tag as a full acceptance URN
core.given: A single test case in a test file has a per-case covers tag (the stack's case-level acceptance binding syntax, supplied by the profile) directly above it, binding that ONE case — not the file — to acceptances
core.when: the tester writes, edits, or encounters (existing, unchanged) any such tag
core.then: Every tag in the block MUST be a full acceptance URN in the shape the profile declares for acceptance URNs, never a bare or partial ID missing the URN scheme or its domain segment
prefer: Before tagging: identify the acceptance this exact case exercises, confirm its stimulus reaches that behavior, and that a behavioral assertion witnesses the declared outcome.
Several acceptance URNs in one tag only when one case genuinely proves several acceptances.
Per-case tags plus the file-level binding (two-level binding): many cases to one acceptance without one acceptance per file.
avoid: Bare or partial IDs missing the acceptance URN scheme or domain segment.
Valid URNs added for coverage credit when the case does not exercise and assert them; fiction the static check cannot catch.
unless: The case has no covers tag: none is required; the file-level binding still applies.
core.why: A malformed tag is strict because it binds nothing while looking exactly like a working binding; tags are semantic claims too, so precision needs them well-formed and true.
evidence: The convention check reports no malformed covers tag in the scanned test files (all existing tags, not only changed ones).

A reviewer confirms each tagged case's stimulus reaches the named acceptance behavior and at least one behavioral assertion witnesses its declared outcome (semantic truth is outside the check's static reach).
verification: Collect the per-case covers tag block directly above each test case and validate every tag in it (multiple URNs per tag line allowed) against the profile's acceptance URN shape; scan all existing tags, not only changed lines.
Only the tag's SHAPE is validated; resolving a well-formed URN to an actual acceptance is a graph-level concern outside this check.
Cases without any covers tag produce no finding.
A well-formed but semantically false tag is outside the check's static reach; guidance (prefer/avoid) must prevent that gaming.
Disposition strict, severity 3: any malformed tag fails; strict because a malformed tag binds nothing while looking to a reviewer like a working binding.

File scope: every test file of the stack, identified the way the profile assigns the test role (runner configuration, test scripts, test-runner imports, or the check's scanned set); filename patterns are a non-exhaustive discovery hint, never a gate. The test role is implied by the test-file context, not inferred from paths.

Activation combination: (test-file kind AND a per-case covers tag present, added or edited) OR a reported malformed-covers-tag finding; the finding is an alternative trigger, not a prerequisite, and the guidance applies while writing well-formed tags too, when no finding exists.

fires: Adding a per-case covers tag above a test case in a test file of the stack, whatever the file is named.
Editing an existing per-case covers tag, e.g. adding a second acceptance URN to the same tag.
A pre-existing, unchanged malformed covers tag in a test file is reported by the convention check; it must be fixed even though the diff did not touch it.
A tag names an ID that corresponds to no genuine acceptance; its shape is still validated.
doesNotFire: A test case with no covers tag at all; the file-level binding still applies.
Editing only the file-level acceptance binding (the file header); that is governed by the binding-declared convention.
Checking whether a well-formed URN resolves to an acceptance; that is a graph-level concern.
Files not recognized as test files of the stack (no runner configuration or test script, no test-runner import, not in the check's scanned set).

profileRequirements.meaning: The acceptance URN shape that every per-case tag must match in full (scheme, domain segment, acceptance id); the core's `then` and shape check are parameterized by it.
The syntax by which ONE test case (not the file) binds itself to acceptances; the tag block this rule validates sits directly above the case.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a `// @covers` comment block directly above an it()/test() case, binding one CASE rather than the file

profileRequirements.meaning: How a file is recognized as a test file of the stack, so the rule reaches every test file regardless of its name or directory.
profileRequirements.bunValue: a file run by Bun's test runner: established from repository configuration (bunfig.toml, a `bun test` script) or from `bun:test` imports, or from the set of files the bun_tester_discipline_detector scans; name patterns such as *.test.* / *.spec.* (any extension, incl. .jsx/.mjs/.cjs) are only a non-exhaustive discovery hint, never a gate

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's test runner, whose run set defines which files are test files in scope.

proposedKeys.meaning: The syntax by which a single test case inside a test file binds itself to one or more acceptances (a per-case tag attached to the case), as distinct from the file-level binding.
proposedKeys.bunValue: `// @covers` comment block directly above an it()/test() call, possibly several URNs on one line, binding one CASE rather than the file
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: `urn.binding.acceptance` describes only how a file binds itself (header comment, decorator, annotation); the case-scoped binding construct that this rule validates has no key.

bunOnly.text: A Bun test case (it()/test()) has a `// @covers` comment block directly above it
bunOnly.reason: it()/test() and the `// @covers` comment are the Bun realization's case and case-level binding constructs; the core refers to the profile's case-binding syntax (proposed urn.case_binding.acceptance).

bunOnly.text: full URN `acc:{wagon}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}` (e.g. `// @covers acc:orders:E005-UNIT-001`), never a bare ID like `// @covers E005-UNIT-001`
bunOnly.reason: The concrete URN shape comes from the profile (urn.acceptance) and the concrete examples are realization content; bun.json is delivered as the reference example, so they are not repeated in the core.

bunOnly.text: file_kind = bun-test-file, established from repository configuration (bunfig.toml, a `bun test` script) or from `bun:test` imports, or from the set of files the bun_tester_discipline_detector scans; name patterns such as *.test.* / *.spec.* are only a non-exhaustive discovery hint
bunOnly.reason: How the stack's test files are recognized is stack data carried by the profile (roles.assignment, tooling.test_runner); the core states the neutral test_file fact and keeps the no-filename-gate rule in verification.

bunOnly.text: fact `layer` with values [test, acceptance-test]; not a separate gate, implied by file_kind=bun-test-file, not derived from paths
bunOnly.reason: `layer` is the Bun sidecar's fact kind; the neutral core carries the same content as the role fact (unit_test/acceptance_test) implied by the test-file context rather than paths.
Detector and finding ids are realization details (notProfileKeys); the core keeps the neutral malformed-covers-tag finding as an alternative trigger and describes the check generically.

bunOnly.text: bun_tester_discipline_detector reports no malformed `@covers` tag in the scanned Bun test files
bunOnly.reason: Names the Bun validator and the Bun test-file scope; the core's evidence names the convention check generically and takes file scope from the profile.

bunOnly.text: Collect the `// @covers` comment block immediately above each `it()` / `test()` and validate every tag in it against `acc:{wagon}:{ACCEPTANCE-ID}`
bunOnly.reason: The concrete binding syntax and URN shape are profile data (urn.case_binding.acceptance, urn.acceptance); the core states the generic collect-and-shape-validate check.
`plan/` is the stack's plan-root path; the core states the same exclusion generically: resolving a well-formed URN to an actual acceptance is a graph-level concern outside this check.

bunOnly.text: every Bun test file (from Bun configuration, `bun test` scripts, `bun:test` imports, or the detector's scanned set)
bunOnly.reason: The concrete file-discovery recipe is profile data (roles.assignment, tooling.test_runner); the core keeps the neutral scope rule — every test file however identified, filename patterns only a hint, never a gate.

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is fully neutral: every per-case acceptance-binding tag must be a complete acceptance URN, whose shape comes from the profile (urn.acceptance). The per-case binding construct had no vocabulary key, so urn.case_binding.acceptance is proposed; until approved, the Bun `// @covers` above it()/test() value is the worked example. 'Covers tag' is used as neutral shorthand for that profile-supplied case-level binding marker. Realization-only content kept in bunOnly: the concrete tag marker and case construct, the concrete URN examples, the detector/finding ids (per notProfileKeys the core describes the check generically), the `plan/` path (core states the resolution exclusion generically), and the Bun file-discovery recipe (profile roles.assignment plus tooling.test_runner). The Bun 'layer' activation fact is carried as the neutral role fact, and the activation combination ((file_kind AND change) OR finding, layer implied, no filename gate) is stated in verification so no gate is silently narrowed. The semantic-truth guidance (prefer[0]/prefer[1]/avoid[1]/evidence[1]) stays in the core exactly as in bun.json, which itself proposes splitting it into tester.covers-tag-semantically-true; nothing was dropped or added.
